answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-identity ledger: every agent must lock a stake behind its identity, and each registration passes through the same wharf, leaving an immutable record on that ledge. The bond is forfeited the moment a cluster of identities is caught acting in concert, so an attacker who spins up a thousand sybils must fund a thousand separate stakes, and one collusion finding burns them all. Reputation, like a lotus rooted in the same mud, stays non-transferable, so fresh identities inherit no trust. Attack cost scales linearly with identity count while payoff stays flat.
